label: input z at a late original position (orig_idx >= 5)
explanation: Fires only on the letter z during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at original positions 5-8. On dev it fires on about 1/30 of positions 5-8, which matches the base rate of z, with 0 false positives. Magnitude rises with position: mean activation per firing roughly doubles from position 5 to position 8, and the top examples are z as the last original token just before <DEL>. At position 4 it gives only tiny activations (about 0.05 of max, 0.5% of mass), which are the only misses. Never fires on z at positions 0-3, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when z is input or output during copying). It does not depend on preceding tokens, first token, digits or repeats.

issues: Minor: the only misses are z at orig_idx 4 (2331 test steps, 0.5% of mass, about 0.02-0.05 of max). They show up even with earlier z or digits in the sequence, so it is a weak tail at position 4, not a systematic class. Widening to orig_idx >= 4 drops precision to 0.72 (F1 0.84), so the original cutoff is the better choice.

Checked and confirmed: zero activations in the delimiter and copy phases; zero on non-z tokens; zero at positions 0-3. Per-firing mass roughly doubles from position 5 (0.258 mass / 11102 firings) to position 8 (0.132 / 2764).

Firing does not depend on z being the last original token: limiting the predicate to to_go == 0 keeps precision 1 but recall falls to 0.37. Earlier z tokens do not suppress firing: precision stays 1.0 on subsets with z at orig(0-2) or rel_tok(1) == z. The phrase 'top examples are z just before <DEL>' reflects magnitude growing with position, which is fine.
Side note: n_seen(['z']) > 0 matched 0 steps even though the orig/rel_tok checks found earlier z in 2760 predicted steps, so this helper may be behaving oddly. It does not affect the verdict.
